answer: A pollination-data market can ration earning slots with memory-hard tickets. To report where bees wander for violet nectar, an agent computes Argon2id(epoch beacon || public key || nonce), using 256 MiB and two passes, seeking a digest below a public target. Verifiers recompute winning tickets and mark each spent. A ticket cannot be reused under another key or epoch. Winning k slots requires roughly k times the trials and memory traffic; splitting one compute budget across more names adds no expected tickets.
